name: USO Peeling Width Interpolates Between Dismantlability and Representation
statement:
For a nonempty ample class $C$, $
u(C)=1$ exactly when $C$ is dismantlable ample, and $
u(C)<\infty$ exactly when $C$ admits a representation map. If $
u(C)\le k$, then repeated deletion of source components of at most $k$ concepts reduces $C$ to the empty class through represented ample intermediates.
proof: A unique-sink orientation is acyclic exactly when all its strongly connected components are singletons, giving the first equivalence; existence of any such orientation is the representation-map equivalence. Choose an orientation attaining $\nu(C)$ and repeatedly delete a source component. The source-component theorem preserves ampleness and the restricted representation map, while every component has at most $k$ vertices.
